description: Check one token contract address in depth. Use it when you hold one address and want the whole picture; to get the official address from a ticker or company name use find_stock_token first. It answers whether the address is in the issuer registry (and, if not, which listed stock its name imitates), the issuer reference price and its age, the latest on-chain price and its premium over that reference, the pool depth (latest.liquidity: the deepest eligible pool in USD, thin below 50,000), the premium history split by US market session, and every gap named. Readings are recorded every 15 minutes (latest.cadence_s), so "latest" is a recorded reading, not a live quote: see latest.age_s. premium compares the latest on-chain price with the issuer reference, whose own age is reference.age_s; when the two are far apart in time, latest.premium_at_reference_time gives the premium of one moment. sources names every source and the pool rule. Every answer opens with one plain sentence; quote it. In the JSON, premium and spread are FRACTIONS (0.01 = 1%; premium > 0 means the on-chain price is above the issuer's), *_age_s and age_s are seconds before generated_at, prices are USD per token. A token is worth `multiplier` shares, and the issuer's reference is already per token. reference.kind: nav_total_return = Coinbase's NAV, token_bid_ask_mid = the mid of Robinhood's token bid/ask. notes are codes for every gap (e.g. reading_stale = our last reading is over 30 min old, pools_capped = the pool count is a minimum). Two chains: base (Coinbase's tokens, symbols end in "c", e.g. NVDAc) and robinhood (Robinhood's, e.g. NVDA). When the user names no chain, call it for both. Facts with their time and source, not advice: https://proofofstock.xyz/docs/legal.md

address.description: the token contract address to check, 0x and 40 hex digits; any token, listed or not

chain.description: which chain and issuer list to check: base (Coinbase's list) or robinhood (Robinhood Chain, Robinhood's list)

hours.description: how many hours back the premium history in `series` (and `series_points`) reaches, 1 to 24 (this server shows at most 24)

include_series.description: also return series_points, the raw premium time series (large); the session medians in `series` are always there

name: stock_passport
